summary: Preserve shared daemon connection waits for errors outside known socket access defects

replay.detail: No replay or stored digest/revision changes.

schema.detail: No database, claim schema or receipt format changes.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or fleet coordination version change.

compatibility.detail: Corrects the connection policy introduced in #2354. For every command using the shared daemon client, the immediate-failure set narrows from all OS-reported Unix connect errors except ENOENT, ECONNREFUSED, EINTR, EAGAIN and ETIMEDOUT to seven known permission/path defects: EPERM, EACCES, EINVAL, ENAMETOOLONG, ENOTDIR, ENOTSOCK and ELOOP. Resource-pressure, lifecycle and other errors retain the existing configured connection wait and follow retry. CLI and first-claim receipt advice points to permissions or the socket path only for known defects; other receipts report the observed OS cause without that attribution. Live daemon-startup observation remains for nondefects and cannot hide a known permission/path defect.

downtime.detail: No migration or required seat restart.

manual.detail: No configuration change, new retry policy or permission override. Ready work remains ready after a failed claim.

recovery.detail: An older build from #2354 retains its broader immediate-failure set and permission/path advice, including for resource-pressure errors. Roll forward to this correction to restore the existing wait behavior for those errors. No data conversion is required.
